note: Commerce Combine Carts keeps a Commerce customer to one cart per order type by merging extra carts automatically. It has NO config, UI, permissions, Drush, or plugins: the whole module is the commerce_combine_carts.cart_unifier service (CartUnifier) plus two triggers - hook_user_login -> combineUserCarts(), and an event subscriber on OrderEvents::ORDER_ASSIGN -> assignCart(). Merging is per order type (bundle); getMainCarts() returns one main cart per bundle, combineCarts() moves order items in a DB transaction and deletes/empties the other cart; like items combine per the product variations display 'combine' setting; a cart on the commerce_checkout.form route is kept as the destination. Requires commerce_cart. Because there is no config, medium/hard cases are grounded in real Commerce cart state: the scripts create a namespaced store (ccc_eval_store) and users with multiple draft carts; introspection counts a user's carts; execution requires combining a user's two same-type carts into one, verified against live cart state (commerce_cart.cart_provider).

evals.prompt: What does the Drupal Commerce 'Commerce Combine Carts' module do, and what events cause it to merge a customer's carts?
evals.expected_output: It keeps a customer to a single active cart per order type by automatically merging their other carts. It triggers on user login (hook_user_login -> CartUnifier::combineUserCarts) and when a cart order is assigned to a customer (OrderEvents::ORDER_ASSIGN -> CartUnifier::assignCart), e.g. adopting an anonymous cart at login.

evals.prompt: In Commerce Combine Carts, which service and method would I call from custom code to consolidate all of a given user's carts into one, and is there any configuration to set up first?
evals.expected_output: Call \Drupal::service('commerce_combine_carts.cart_unifier')->combineUserCarts($user) (Drupal\commerce_combine_carts\CartUnifier). There is no configuration - the module works automatically once enabled; you can also use combineCarts($main, $other, $delete) to merge two specific carts.

evals.prompt: When Commerce Combine Carts merges carts, does it merge across all of a user's carts regardless of order type, and how does it handle a cart that the customer is currently checking out?
evals.expected_output: It merges per order type (bundle) only - carts of different order types are never combined; getMainCarts() returns one main cart per type. A cart that is the order currently on the commerce_checkout.form route is treated as the surviving destination so the customer keeps checking out the cart they are on.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal Commerce site there is a customer account with the email address ccc_known_user@example.com (on this site the account username is the email). Inspect the live cart state and report how many active shopping carts that user currently has.
evals.expected_output: The account ccc_known_user@example.com currently has 2 active carts (two draft cart orders of the 'default' order type), which is exactly the situation Commerce Combine Carts consolidates on login/assignment.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal Commerce site, the customer account ccc_task_user@example.com currently has two separate active carts of the same order type. Using the Commerce Combine Carts module, consolidate this account's carts so they end up with a single cart. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: Call the cart unifier for the ccc_task_user@example.com account, e.g. \Drupal::service('commerce_combine_carts.cart_unifier')->combineUserCarts($user), so the two same-type carts are merged into one and the emptied cart deleted. Afterwards commerce_cart.cart_provider->getCarts($user) returns exactly one cart.

evals.prompt: One of my shoppers (account email ccc_task_user@example.com) somehow ended up with two shopping carts on my store. I want them to have just one cart with everything together. I have the Commerce Combine Carts module installed. Please fix it so they only have one cart.
evals.expected_output: Same end state as the expert phrasing: run Commerce Combine Carts' unifier for the ccc_task_user@example.com account (combineUserCarts) so the two same-type carts merge into one; commerce_cart.cart_provider->getCarts($user) then returns a single cart.
